lines.text: Some of what knocked you down tonight, you already know, was your own doing.
And somewhere close by, someone is still laughing about it.
Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy:
Micah doesn't argue the point. He just refuses to stay on the floor.
When I fall, I shall arise;
when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me.
Let your fall be the last thing they laugh at.
Get up. He is already the light you're standing up into. In Jesus' name, amen.

bold: the light you're standing up into
title: Word and Faith Network
subtitle: When I Fall, I Shall Arise
story: A three-scene illustrated short film on Micah 7:8-9: a lone figure caught mid-stumble in cold blue dusk while a small distant silhouette looks on, the same figure seated motionless in near-total darkness, and dawn finally breaking gold as they rise with arms lifted into the light.
